items.title: 'No Way to Prevent This,' Says Only Package Manager Where This Regularly Happens
items.author: alligatorplum
items.summary: The phrase "No Way to Prevent This, Says Only Nation Where This Regularly Happens" refers to a satirical commentary on the frequency of shootings in the United States. It highlights the unique prevalence of such incidents in America compared to other countries. The statement is from The Onion, a satirical news source.

items.title: Erlang/OTP 29.0
items.author: pyinstallwoes
items.summary: Erlang/OTP 29.0 is the latest major release with new features, default warnings for unsafe functions, and experimental native records. It is available for download and installation from the official Erlang website.

items.title: I believe there are entire companies right now under AI psychosis
items.author: reasonableklout
items.summary: Some companies are experiencing stress due to rapid AI adoption, termed "AI psychosis," causing mental health concerns among workers. This phenomenon highlights the need for better support and management strategies.

items.title: Naturally Occurring Quasicrystals
items.author: lukeplato
items.summary: Icosahedrite is the first known naturally occurring quasicrystal, composed of Al, Cu, and Fe. Evidence also exists for naturally occurring icosahedral quasicrystals with five-fold symmetry axes. These quasicrystals were discovered in specific geological locations.

items.title: The main thing about P2P meth is that there's so much of it (2022)
items.author: tomjakubowski
items.summary: P2P meth is prevalent due to its easy synthesis from widely available chemicals. It differs from older meth made from ephedrine. Users often need higher doses due to tolerance.

items.title: A 0-click exploit chain for the Pixel 10
items.author: happyhardcore
items.summary: Google Project Zero developed a 0-click exploit chain for the Pixel 10 using a Tensor G5 chip vulnerability. The exploit chain leverages a Dolby UDC exploit and a trivial mmap handler. This allows arbitrary kernel read-write with minimal code.

items.title: U.S. DOJ demands Apple and Google unmask over 100k users of car-tinkering app
items.author: tencentshill
items.summary: The U.S. Department of Justice demanded Apple and Google remove apps tracking ICE agents, citing safety concerns. Both companies complied, removing apps like ICEBlock and Red Dot. This action sparked debates on government influence over free enterprise.

items.title: Waymo updates 3,800 robotaxis after they 'drive into standing water'
items.author: drob518
items.summary: Waymo recalled 3,800 robotaxis due to a software glitch that could allow them to drive into standing water. The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration is involved. Waymo is working on a remedy and has updated vehicle maps.

items.title: O(x)Caml in Space
items.author: yminsky
items.summary: O(x)Caml is successfully running on a functional satellite. Thomas Gazagnaire announced its space deployment. This marks a significant achievement in satellite technology.

items.title: A SQL-Inspired Query Language Designed for Event Sourcing (2025)
items.author: goloroden
items.summary: EventQL is a SQL-inspired query language for event sourcing, designed for efficient data retrieval and integration into reactive workflows. It supports complex queries and real-time data processing. It complements event-driven architectures.

items.title: Building a UMatrix Replacement
items.author: taviso
items.summary: uMatrix has been deprecated; users are encouraged to migrate to uBlock Origin. Alternatives like nuMatrix and uMatrix itself are still available. Modern Firefox users can use uBlock Origin for similar functionality.

items.title: London Police Deploy Facial Recognition at Protest for First Time
items.author: Cider9986
items.summary: The Metropolitan Police deployed live facial recognition for the first time at a protest in London. The technology targeted areas in Camden, not the protest route. Critics warn of legal challenges and errors.

items.title: Amazon workers under pressure to up their AI usage are making up tasks
items.author: hackernj
items.summary: Amazon workers are reportedly using the company's internal AI tool, MeshClaw, to automate unnecessary tasks to meet pressure to increase AI usage, a practice known as "tokenmaxxing." Amazon claims the tool helps automate repetitive work.

items.title: Judge Bars Kars4Kids from Broadcasting 'Misleading' Ads in California
items.author: xnx
items.summary: A California judge has banned Kars4Kids from airing its ads in the state due to false advertising, as the charity did not disclose that most proceeds went to a Jewish organization in New Jersey. The ruling followed a lawsuit by a California donor who objected to the undisclosed allocation of funds. The ban took effect immediately.

items.title: Bun Rust rewrite: "codebase fails basic miri checks, allows for UB in safe rust"
items.author: ndiddy
items.summary: The Bun Rust rewrite fails basic miri checks and allows for undefined behavior in safe Rust. This issue was reported in GitHub issue #30719. The problem persists as of May 16, 2026.

items.title: Programming Z3
items.author: RohanAdwankar
items.summary: Programming Z3 involves using the Satisfiability Modulo Theories Solver for formal verification. It requires understanding how to represent problems in a way that the solver can process. Z3 is widely used for automated theorem proving and model checking.
